summary: Short-range correlations and mean-field degeneracy in low-energy Au+Au; identified-hadron flow decorrelations as nuclear-shape probes; Lorentz-aware self-supervised jet representations. Latest announcement batch, with submissions approximately 25 to 39 hours before this run.

papers.title: Sampling nucleon short-range correlations in coordinate and momentum space for Au+Au collision simulations
papers.short_authors: Yu-Jing Huang, Qian-Ru Lin, Long-Gang Pang
papers.summary: At 2.4 GeV, a correlated nuclear initialization changes charged-pion and kaon yields. Controlled variations indicate that the high-momentum single-nucleon distribution drives the pion change, while a refitted mean field can counteract it.
papers.abstract: A correlated initialization combining spatial and momentum structure, proton-neutron pair assignments and high-momentum components is implemented in SMASH. Tests separate contributions to pion production and investigate compensation by the mean field and kaon production.
papers.assessment: Strong diagnostic with controlled ingredient tests and data-guided recalibration. The compensation is model- and calibration-dependent, not an isolated measurement of short-range correlations; the initial submission predates the strict 24-hour window.

papers.title: Revealing Nuclear Shape through Identified-Hadron Flow Decorrelations
papers.short_authors: Hadi Mehrabpour, Abhisek Saha, Li Yan
papers.summary: Hydrodynamics plus hadronic transport predicts that crossing points of pion-kaon and pion-proton flow-factorization ratios respond differently to quadrupole deformation and triaxiality in U+U and Ne+Ne.
papers.abstract: The authors propose identified-hadron flow decorrelations and their crossing coordinates as complementary probes of nuclear shape, studying deformation and collision-energy dependence using event-by-event hydrodynamics and hadronic transport.
papers.assessment: A specific, testable observable with comparisons across species and systems, but it is a model prediction, not a nuclear-shape measurement. Detector acceptance, statistical reach, nonflow, reference selection, and sensitivity to evolution assumptions require validation.

papers.title: Lorentz symmetry in self-supervised representation learning
papers.short_authors: Andreas Hermansen, Tobias Golling, Slava Voloshynovskiy
papers.summary: LeJEPA self-supervised pretraining on 100 million simulated JetClass jets is combined with a Lorentz-equivariant transformer and compared with several representation-learning baselines. The authors report stronger probe and downstream performance.
papers.abstract: The study combines symmetry-aware architectures or physics-motivated augmentations with self-supervised jet representation learning, comparing pretrained models against other objectives and training from scratch on jet benchmarks.
papers.assessment: Substantive baselines, ablations and downstream tasks make this a credible HEP method study. Heavy-ion jet transfer is speculative: underlying-event contamination, detector response and domain shifts require dedicated validation; the paper was submitted about 25 hours before the run.
